title: The Trifid Nebula
caption: The Trifid Nebula, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at La Silla
celestial: Trifid Nebula · constellation Sagittarius · about 5500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #70 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Dark bands of dust cut across the glowing heart of this nebula, dividing it into three parts. That is where the Trifid Nebula gets its name. This massive star factory was photographed with the Wide Field Imager camera on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory in northern Chile.

The Trifid is unusual because it combines three types of nebula in one. Textbooks usually sort nebulae into three kinds. In emission nebulae, gas glows because young stars energise it. In reflection nebulae, dust scatters nearby starlight, and in dark nebulae, dense dust blocks light from behind.

Together the three show the violence of newly born stars and hint that more stars will form, since the dusty regions hold material for future stars. The image covers a field of approximately 13 by 17 arcminutes.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (13.89 x 22.82 arcminutes) and distance (5500 light years), the frame spans roughly 22 × 37 light-years. Its light set out about 5,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and R filters with a hydrogen filter. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the nebula's colours and faint gas are much more vivid here than through an eyepiece.

alt: A glowing nebula divided into three parts by dark bands of dust.
